summary: Courtenay Bay Breakwater Light: a red light on a concrete tower built in 1944 as a wartime gun-battery post made to look like a lighthouse, at the end of a Saint John Harbour breakwater.

structures.note: Original light on a small wooden tower (Rowlett). Light moved 46 m (150 ft) shoreward and re-erected on the breakwater in 1928 (LighthouseFriends). Build date not given.

Steel-reinforced concrete fire control post designed and built to look like a lighthouse (NBMHP); Rowlett calls it a faux lighthouse, 10 m octagonal; CCG list 9.9 m, white hexagonal with red top. Lantern and aluminum panels added 2018. Current light is shown from its top.

staffing.note: Unwatched white light when first established (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Accessible only by boat (Rowlett). Grounds and tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Breakwater extension of 2,500 feet (760 m) completed (LighthouseFriends).
Unwatched white light established at the outer end of the breakwater (LighthouseFriends); Rowlett gives station established 1927.
Light moved 150 feet (46 m) shoreward and re-erected on the breakwater (LighthouseFriends).
After war was declared, a WWI 18-pounder gun and automobile spotlights were placed on the breakwater (NBMHP).
Concrete fire control post built to look like a lighthouse; the 18-pounder was replaced by a twin 6-pounder in June 1944 (NBMHP; Rowlett).
Battery decommissioned after the war and mostly dismantled (LighthouseFriends; NBMHP says dismantled in 1946).
Canadian Coast Guard added aluminum siding and a lantern room, and upgraded the light (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).

corrections.why: The record's 1946 is the year the battery was mostly dismantled and the year Rowlett's entry heading gives with a question mark ('1946 (?)'). NBMHP says the concrete fire control post was designed and built in June 1944, and Rowlett's text says the present tower was built as a faux lighthouse in 1944.

The CCG List of Lights places the light at 45 15 26.4 N, 066 02 42.2 W, near the outer end of the breakwater. The record uses an OpenStreetMap point about 40 m away. LighthouseFriends gives 45.257333, -66.045056. For human review.

notes_for_editor: Not read: the CBC News report of 27 April 2018 that LighthouseFriends cites (the CBC page timed out twice; the story's 2018 work rests on LighthouseFriends and Rowlett). fortwiki.com returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Corpus Marine reports end with fiscal 1923-24, so the 1927 establishment, the 1928 move and the 1919 extension come only from LighthouseFriends and Rowlett. Disputes left open: (a) signal: CCG list Iso R 2s versus Rowlett and LighthouseFriends red flash every 4 s (record's OSM value is Fl R 4s); (b) focal height 13.0 m (CCG) versus 13.5 m focal plane (Rowlett); (c) tower shape: hexagonal (CCG, LighthouseFriends) versus octagonal (Rowlett). Not known: when the wooden light came down and when the light moved to the battery tower (Rowlett says after 1945). The 1913-14 and 1923-24 Marine items are described in the reports' own lists; neither gives a date for the works. No keepers were found, which matches LighthouseFriends' 'unwatched'. No people named in sources beyond the agencies, so no names are published.
